content.comment_body: Hello, I'm just starting with [product_name] and noticed that the mathematical instruction doesn't match my timer settings correctly. I set it to 20 seconds, but it returns 1999 instead of 2000. Not sure if this is a simulation issue or something else, and adjusting it might cause issues throughout my looped logic. It's my first post, so I'm not sure if I'm asking correctly.
Sorry, I couldn't understand your issue. You haven't explained how you connect the timer to the mathematical instruction. Please upload your project in a ZIP archive.

I've realized now that the issue isn't with the mathematical instruction, but with the Chronometer. In the screenshot, when I press I1 for one second, it activates the timer for 20 seconds but the Chronometer reads 1995ms instead of 2000. I could use B002 in seconds, but I need high precision, especially when I manually activate I1 for more than two seconds.
I don't fully understand the logic in your program, but that's not crucial. The main problem seems to be that you're testing your program only in the simulation—not on actual [product_name] hardware.
Check out the attached screen recording from the Online Test.

analysis.insight_summary: A user encountered a mismatch between expected and measured timer values in milliseconds within the simulation of [product_name], where a 20-second timer is interpreted as slightly less than 2000 ms by the Chronometer. The user is concerned about timing precision and synchronization in their looped logic, especially when manually triggering timers.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects that the timer and Chronometer within the simulation will accurately reflect millisecond-level timing, allowing reliable testing and validation of their logic before deploying it on actual hardware.
